name: uniq
description: Filters adjacent repeated lines: removes, counts, or shows duplicates.

flags.description: Prefix lines with the number of occurrences.
Compare only the first N characters.

examples.explanation: Removes duplicates. uniq only compares adjacent lines, so input must be sorted first.
The classic frequency ranking: count repetitions, sort numerically, take the top hits.
Shows only the lines that appear more than once in a row.

about: uniq compares neighboring lines only. The sort | uniq -c | sort -rn pipeline is one of the most useful idioms on Linux for "what appears most often". For unsorted data, awk '!seen[$0]++' is a common alternative.
useCases: Count and rank IP addresses, URLs, or error types.
Remove duplicate entries from sorted lists.
mistakes: Running uniq without sorting first — non-adjacent duplicates survive.
